text:
support-ops: ACME just escalated — p99 on /v1/generate shot up to ~1.2s starting 11:04 UTC. No 5xxs, just tail latency. Customer SLA hit.

maria: Copy. Tenant acme-123? Any recent deploys or config changes?

support-ops: Yes — rolled continuous-batcher config change at 10:58 UTC: max_batch_size=64, hold_timeout_ms=50, grace_window_ms=20. No other infra deploys in that time window.

aj: Looking at metrics now. p95 moved 120ms -> 620ms, p99 240ms -> 1.25s. Batch size distribution shifted — many small prompts are now waiting much longer to fill batches.

lucas: That matches a theory — larger max_batch_size + nonzero hold timeout can create long waits for low-rate traffic. Can we hotfix?

maria: Suggestion: instead of full revert, reduce max_batch_size to 12 and drop hold_timeout_ms to 8ms for small-prompt routes. Also bump grace_window_ms to 40ms to avoid coalesce thrash.

oncall: I'm starting a canary: applying hold_timeout_ms=8, max_batch_size=12 to two pods in shard-us-east-1. Monitoring p95/p99 for acme-123.

sre-bot: Deploy event: canary-config -> batcher-v2 applied to hosts batch-12-1 and batch-12-2.

sre-bot: Observed metrics (60s): acme-123 p99 on canary hosts dropped from 1.25s -> 210ms, p95 -> 150ms.

support-ops: Customer confirmed improvement on the canary hosts. Good. What's the root cause — why did a 50ms hold timeout cause a huge tail?

aj: Quick root cause hypothesis: traffic shape is many tiny bursts (short prompts) with inter-arrival jitter. With max_batch_size 64, the head request in a batch can wait for slow arrivals up to hold_timeout_ms. When requests come in microbursts, grace_window_ms=20 caused aggressive coalescing flushes that sometimes leave a lonely head request stuck while subsequent groups re-coalesce, producing head_linger spikes. We saw coalesce_wait percentiles at 99.9% ~900-1200ms in traces.

infra-admin: Also noted occasional GC pause spikes (~120ms) on a subset of hosts around the same time — likely amplified the effect but not root cause.

lucas: Action plan proposed:
- immediate: roll global defaults back to safer values (max_batch_size=16, hold_timeout_ms=10)
- short term: per-tenant adaptive batch sizing and smaller hold windows for low-rate tenants
- telemetry: add alert on head_linger_ms > 200ms and coalesce_wait p99 > 300ms
- followup: run traffic-sim tests for microburst patterns before changing global defaults

maria: I applied the temporary global mitigation: max_batch_size=16, hold_timeout_ms=10, grace_window_ms=40 (rolled 100% at 11:22 UTC). Documented in the runbook under "batcher/hold-timeout-mitigation".

support-ops: Updating ACME ticket with mitigation and ETA for full rollback/patch.

aj: Repro script for the pattern (run from a test box):
```
while true; do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":8}' >/dev/null &
  sleep 0.02
done
```
Hit ~50-60 RPS with 20ms spacing, observe p99 jump when batcher is in aggressive batching mode.

support-ops: Logs snippet from batcher around the spike: 
```
[11:04:12.842] batcher INFO shard=us-east-1 tenant=acme-123 batch_size=1 coalesce_wait=1024ms head_linger=1024ms
[11:04:12.943] batcher INFO shard=us-east-1 tenant=acme-123 batch_size=32 flush_reason=timeout
```

maria: Nice logs. I'll add a short unit/ integration test to the change-review: simulate low-rate short-prompt distribution and assert p99 < 500ms on canary before rollout.

oncall: After the global rollback, acme p99 back to ~180-220ms across clusters. Monitoring for 30m.

lucas: Postmortem/action items assigned: AUTOGEN-442 (revert-safe-config), AUTOGEN-443 (per-tenant adaptive batcher), AUTOGEN-444 (batcher telemetry alerts), AUTOGEN-445 (traffic-sim test).

support-ops: I'll close the escalation once we see 30m of stable telemetry and customer ack. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

maria: Leaving notes in the runbook and PR to require a traffic-sim run for any batcher config changes going forward.

aj: For completeness — if we need immediate temporary relief in future: set hold_timeout_ms=0 (fast flush) for affected tenant or route, or enable instant-flush-on-small-payloads. Both reduce batching efficiency but avoid tail spikes.

infra-admin: I'll put a scheduled job to run the microburst traffic test nightly against staging to catch regressions.

sre-bot: Incident closed to monitoring (will auto-resolve if no regressions in 30m).
